subject: combined-science
title: Physics — Power
meta_desc: GCSE Combined Science (AQA) practice covering Physics — Power, specification section 4.1.1.4.
final_note: You worked through Physics — Power — 11 specification statements.

concepts.def: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred, or the rate at which work is done. It is not a quantity of energy: it says how many joules are transferred each second, so a power value always needs both an energy and a time.
The watt is the unit of power, symbol W. An energy transfer of 1 joule per second is equal to a power of 1 watt, so 1 W is 1 J/s.
The energy transferred, symbol E, is measured in joules, J. Divided by the time in seconds it gives the power: power = (energy transferred)/(time), [P = E/t].

Work done, symbol W, is measured in joules, J, because doing work is one way of transferring energy. Divided by the time it gives the power: power = (work done)/(time), [P = W/t]. The letter W is also the symbol for the watt; in P = W/t it stands for the work done.
The time, symbol t, is measured in seconds, s. A time given in minutes or hours must be converted to seconds before it is used in P = E/t or P = W/t.

Two machines that transfer the same energy, for example two electric motors lifting the same weight through the same height, differ in power only through the time taken. The one that finishes sooner has the greater power.

mcqs.q: Which statement gives the definition of power?
options: The rate at which energy is transferred or work is done
The total amount of energy that a device transfers
The time that an energy transfer takes to finish
The force that a machine uses to shift a load
mcqs.explain: This is the definition in the specification: power is a rate, so an energy and a time are both involved.

mcqs.q: Which word equation for power is given in the specification?
options: power = energy transferred x time
power = time taken / energy transferred
power = energy transferred / the time
power = the work done x time taken
mcqs.explain: Matches power = (energy transferred)/(time), written in symbols as P = E/t.

mcqs.q: In the equation P = E/t, which units should be used for E and for t?
options: energy in newtons and time in seconds
energy in joules and time in seconds
energy in watts and time in seconds
energy in joules and time in hours
mcqs.explain: The specification gives energy transferred, E, in joules, J, and time, t, in seconds, s.

mcqs.q: An energy transfer of 1 joule per second is equal to a power of:
options: 1 joule
60 watts
1 kilowatt
1 watt
mcqs.explain: This is the statement in the specification: 1 joule per second is a power of 1 watt.

mcqs.q: A kettle transfers 360 000 J of energy in 180 s. What is its power?
mcqs.explain: P = E/t = 360 000 / 180 = 2000 W, that is 2000 joules transferred every second.

mcqs.q: A crane does 90 000 J of work in 30 s. What is the power of the crane?
mcqs.explain: P = W/t = 90 000 / 30 = 3000 W, using power = (work done)/(time).

mcqs.q: Two electric motors lift identical loads through the same height. Motor A takes 4 s and motor B takes 10 s. Which statement is correct?
options: Motor A is more powerful, because it must have done extra work on the load
Motor B is more powerful, because it keeps working for a longer time
Both motors have equal power, because the work done on the load is equal
Motor A is more powerful, because it does the same work in a shorter time
mcqs.explain: Equal loads through equal heights means equal work done, so the shorter time gives the greater power.

mcqs.q: A 1500 W heater is switched on for 300 s. How much energy does it transfer?
options: 5 J
mcqs.explain: Rearranging P = E/t gives E = Pt = 1500 x 300 = 450 000 J.

mcqs.q: The specification gives the equation P = W/t. What does W stand for in this equation?
options: the power in watts, as W is its unit
the work done, measured in newtons
the weight lifted, in newtons
the work done, measured in joules
mcqs.explain: The specification pairs work done, W, with joules, J; power is the work done divided by the time.

mcqs.q: A motor transfers 15 000 J of energy in 2 minutes. What is its power?
mcqs.explain: 2 minutes is 120 s, so P = E/t = 15 000 / 120 = 125 W.

mcqs.q: A lamp transfers 500 J of energy while a pump does 500 J of work. Which statement about the units is correct?
options: Both are in joules, because doing work is a way of transferring energy
Work done is in newtons, so the two quantities cannot be compared
Energy transferred is in watts, so only the work is in joules
Energy transferred is in joules but work done is in watts
mcqs.explain: The specification gives energy transferred, E, in joules, and work done, W, in joules.

mcqs.q: Two cranes lift the same load to the same height. Crane X takes 20 s and crane Y takes 50 s. Which quantity is different for the two cranes?
options: the work done on the load
the energy passed to the load
the power of the two cranes
the weight of the loads lifted
mcqs.explain: The same work done in different times means different rates of transfer, so the powers differ.
